text.marquee: RANK UP CITY · BUILDING 3 · THE DETECTIVE AGENCY
text.tagline:
Read the clues. Question the witnesses.
Find the cat.
text.taglineEs: Lee las pistas, ordena los hechos y deduce. Suma patitas <ico-paw></ico-paw> en cada ronda.
text.help: Easy: read the clue or listen to the witness. Then pick the right answer, put the events in order, or tap the words to build the sentence. Stuck? Tap Totti's nose for a hint. He hates it, so use it wisely.
text.bossWin: Case closed! Enri was at the Grand Hotel the whole time, asleep on a room-service cart. You found him, detective. You rank up to B2, and the official B1 exam is waiting for you.
text.gameOver: The trail went cold. It happens to every detective. Take a breath and reopen the file.
text.good: Good work, detective. Priya is impressed, and she's hard to impress. Your prize is waiting. Claim it!
text.ok: That was a tough day on the case. Run it back for a better card, or claim your prize anyway.

boss.name: DETECTIVE TOTTI
boss.quote: I solved it. You helped. Slightly.

epic.name: THE EVIDENCE BOARD
epic.quote: Must be, might be, can't be.

common.name: CASE FILE
common.quote: Every case starts with one question. Run it back!

hint.name: TOTTI
hint.label: TOTTI'S NOSE
hint.post: ...Do not make me do that again.

s1.name: The briefing
s1.intro: Detective! Priya's agency needs you. Enri, the cat who never moves, has gone. His cushion at the café is still warm. Your partner is Totti: he gives the hints, and he hates it. First, the briefing. What has happened, and what hasn't happened yet?

rounds.line: Right, everyone. Enri is missing. Has anyone seen him today?
options: No, I haven't seen him since last night.
No, I didn't see him since last night.
No, I haven't seen him yesterday.
rounds.retryLine: From last night until now. Use the present perfect, and since.
rounds.thanks: Nobody has. Since last night. That's our starting point.

rounds.line: Mia left this note on the counter. Read it.

doc.title: MIA'S NOTE
doc.html:
8:15 a.m.

I've already served breakfast, but I haven't seen the orange cat yet. His cushion is still warm.

— Mia

options: No, she hasn't seen him yet.
Yes, she saw him at breakfast.
Yes, she has just fed him.
rounds.retryLine: Read the note again. Look at the word yet.
rounds.thanks: Good. Breakfast has happened. Enri hasn't.

rounds.line: Mia says he never goes anywhere. Put it in one sentence for the case file.
rounds.answer: He has never left the café
rounds.retryLine: Have or has, then never, then the past participle.
rounds.thanks: Never. Not once in four years. Until now.

rounds.line: Everyone's here: Mia, Jack, Marcos. You run the meeting. How do you start?
options: Let's go around the table. Mia, would you like to start?
Everybody talk now, please.
Let's to go around the table. Mia, you start.
rounds.retryLine: Politely. Give each person a turn.
rounds.thanks: Nicely done. Mia, go ahead.

rounds.line: Here's the café log from this morning. Something on it hasn't happened yet.

doc.title: CAFÉ LOG · TUESDAY
doc.html:
7:00 — Mia has opened the café.

7:10 — The empty bread boxes have already come back from the Grand Hotel.

7:30 — Enri's bowl is still full. He hasn't eaten yet.

rounds.q: Which of these has NOT happened yet?
options: Enri has eaten his breakfast.
Mia has opened the café.
The bread boxes have come back.
rounds.retryLine: Look for not and yet in the log.
rounds.thanks: His bowl is full. Enri never misses breakfast.

s2.name: The witnesses
s2.intro: Time to question the witnesses. They'll tell you what they were doing when something happened: was drinking, was closing, heard, saw. Listen for the order of events.

rounds.line: Last night? I was drinking my tea when I heard a noise outside. A sort of bump. Then nothing.
rounds.note: For the case file: what was Jack doing when he heard the noise?
options: He was drinking his tea.
He drank his tea after the noise.
He was hearing a noise.
rounds.retryLine: What was I doing? The long action, mate. The one that got interrupted.
rounds.thanks: Right. Cold tea, and a bump in the dark.

rounds.line: This morning was normal at first. I opened the café at seven. I was cleaning the counter when I heard the back door. That was the bread boxes. Then I saw the empty cushion.
rounds.retryLine: Listen again. What came first?
rounds.thanks: That's my morning, exactly.

rounds.line: Two statements about ten o'clock last night. They can't both be true.

statements.text: I was reading inside all evening.
I saw Jack at the newspaper stand at ten.

rounds.evidence: Jack's umbrella, by the door. It's still damp. The rain stopped at half past ten.
rounds.retryLine: Look at the umbrella again. Who was out in the rain?
rounds.thanks: Right. Jack was outside at ten. He isn't lying: he forgot he went out for the newspaper.

rounds.line: And before all that, last night, something strange happened while I was closing. Say it for the file.
rounds.answer: I was closing the café when the lights went out
alts: The lights went out when I was closing the café
rounds.retryLine: The long action first: I was closing. Then when, and the short action.
rounds.thanks: Two minutes of darkness. And then the lights came back.

rounds.line: Let's put last night in order. Jack went out for a newspaper at ten. Before that, at nine, the truck left. The lights went out a little earlier, while Mia was closing. And Jack heard a noise while he was drinking his tea, just before the truck left.
events: Jack went out in the rain.
rounds.hint: earliest first: the lights went out while Mia was closing
rounds.retryLine: Careful. Before that, earlier, just before: follow the clock, not my sentences.
rounds.thanks: Lights out, a bump, the truck, the rain. Now we have a night.

s3.name: The evidence board
s3.tag: Must, might, can't & disagreeing with tact
s3.intro: The evidence board. How sure can you be? Must be, might be, can't be. And when a witness says something you don't agree with, disagree with tact.

rounds.line: Pin number one. How sure can we be?
rounds.evidence: Enri's cushion is still warm, and the café doors have been locked all night.
options: He must be near.
He can't be near.
He might be in another city.
rounds.retryLine: Warm means recent. Locked doors. So?
rounds.thanks: Must be near. Unless somebody else has been sitting on that cushion…

rounds.line: Pin number two. Vera never liked that cat.
rounds.evidence: The Grand Hotel's cameras show Vera in the lobby from eight until midnight.
options: It must be Vera.
It can't be Vera.
It might be Vera.
rounds.retryLine: She was on camera all night. So?
rounds.thanks: Vera is off the board.

rounds.line: Frankly, that cat was a menace. The street is quieter without him.
options: I take your point, but I see it differently. The whole street misses him.
You're wrong, and you're rude.
I am agree with you, but no.
rounds.retryLine: Rude, darling. Try again, with manners.
rounds.thanks: Hm. Diplomatic. Perhaps the street is a little too quiet.

rounds.line: Pin number three. Mia found something by the back door.
rounds.evidence: There is orange hair inside one of the empty bread boxes. Last night, the boxes went to the Grand Hotel.
options: He might be at the hotel.
He must be in the café.
He can't be at the hotel.
rounds.retryLine: Hair in a box is a possibility, not proof.
rounds.thanks: Possible. Not certain. Not yet.

rounds.line: So what do we do next? Suggest it. Don't order it.
rounds.answer: It might be worth checking the truck
rounds.retryLine: Softer. It might be worth, plus the -ing form.
rounds.thanks: Agreed. Tonight, we follow the bread.

s4.name: The stakeout
s4.intro: Stakeout time. Plans, predictions and conditions: we're going to, if he comes back, unless we hurry. Grab a coffee. It's going to be a long night.

rounds.line: It's six o'clock. We've decided what to do. So, detective: what's the plan?
options: We're going to watch the café tonight.
We will watching the café tonight.
We watch the café tonight, maybe.
rounds.retryLine: It's already decided. A plan: going to.
rounds.thanks: Good. I'll bring the coffee. You bring the cat treats.

rounds.line: And what if Enri simply comes back on his own?
rounds.answer: If he comes back we will see him
alts: We will see him if he comes back
rounds.retryLine: A real possibility: if plus the present, then will.
rounds.thanks: Exactly. And if he doesn't, we follow the truck.

rounds.line: Here's the delivery schedule. Read it quickly.

doc.title: DELIVERY SCHEDULE · NEON CAFÉ → GRAND HOTEL
doc.html:
Every night: the truck collects the bread boxes at the café at 9:00 p.m.

It arrives at the Grand Hotel kitchen at 10:00 p.m.

The empty boxes come back at 7:10 a.m.

rounds.q: When does the truck arrive at the hotel?
options: At ten p.m.
At nine p.m.
At ten past seven in the morning.
rounds.retryLine: Arrives, not leaves. Read it again.
rounds.thanks: Ten o'clock. An hour in a warm truck. Hm.

rounds.line: It's cold and wet out there. Think like a cat. Where would you go?
options: If I were a cat, I would go somewhere warm.
If I am a cat, I would go somewhere warm.
If I were a cat, I will go somewhere warm.
rounds.retryLine: You're not a cat. It's imaginary: if I were, then would.
rounds.thanks: Somewhere warm. Like a box of fresh bread.

rounds.line: It's ten to nine! The truck leaves at nine!
rounds.answer: Unless we hurry we will miss the truck
alts: We will miss the truck unless we hurry
rounds.retryLine: Unless means if not. No don't after it.
rounds.thanks: Then run! I'll drive.

sb.name: The reveal
sb.intro: This is it, detective: the reveal. Everyone is at the agency, and you present the case. Everything you've learned: what has happened, the order of the night, how sure you are, and the plan that worked. Find that cat, and you rank up to B2.

rounds.line: First, the true order of last night. The truck arrived at the Grand Hotel at ten. It left the café at nine. Earlier, while Mia was closing, the lights went out, and in the dark, Enri climbed into a warm bread box.
events: The lights went out while Mia was closing.
Enri climbed into a warm bread box.
The truck arrived at the Grand Hotel.
rounds.hint: follow the clock: the lights went out first
rounds.retryLine: Follow the clock, not my sentences. What happened first?
rounds.thanks: Exactly. That's the night, in the right order.

rounds.line: Now the hotel kitchen. Where is Enri?
rounds.evidence: Last night the hotel kitchen received five bread boxes. One had a hole in the lid, orange hair inside, and half a croissant.
options: He must be at the hotel.
He might be at the café.
He can't be at the hotel.
rounds.retryLine: A hole, orange hair, half a croissant. How sure are you?
rounds.thanks: Must be. The kitchen staff say a cat has been asleep on a room-service cart since midnight.

rounds.line: One more thing. Who kept Enri's cushion warm? Two statements. One of them can't be true.

statements.text: I wasn't at the café this morning.
The cushion was still warm at seven.

rounds.evidence: The café door camera, 6:40 a.m.: a cat comes in through the cat flap, sleeps on the orange cushion and leaves at 6:58. It's Totti.
rounds.retryLine: Look at the camera again. Who came in at six forty?
rounds.thanks: Totti says six forty is still night. For a cat, maybe. Not a lie: a mix-up. And now we know why the cushion was warm.

rounds.line: Mia, Jack, Marcos, even Vera. Everyone's listening. The floor is yours, detective.
options: Thanks for coming, everyone. Let's start with what we know.
Listen to me. I am the detective.
Thanks for come, everyone. We start.
rounds.retryLine: Open it like a meeting. Thank them, then start.
rounds.thanks: Go on. Nobody is even looking at their phone.

rounds.line: Now the conclusion, for the file. One sentence.
rounds.answer: Enri has been at the Grand Hotel since last night
rounds.retryLine: From last night until now: has been, and since.
rounds.thanks: Case closed. Somebody tell Totti. He'll pretend he wasn't worried.
